questions.title: What exactly makes NF4 'information-theoretically optimal' for normally distributed weights?
questions.question_body: The paper says 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) is 'information theoretically optimal' for zero-mean normal distributions. What is the precise objective being optimized here? Is it minimizing expected quantization MSE under $X \sim N(0,1)$, minimizing KL divergence between original and quantized distributions, or maximizing entropy of bin occupancy? A short derivation or citation for why equal expected occupancy of bins is optimal under a specific loss would help.

questions.title: Why does NF4 use absolute max scaling if the codebook is derived from $N(0,1)$ quantiles?
questions.question_body: NF4 builds a codebook using quantiles of $N(0,1)$ and then says to map weights into $[-1,1]$ using absolute max rescaling at the block level. If the codebook assumes a standard normal, why is absmax scaling (which depends on extrema, not standard deviation) the right mapping? The text claims step (3) is 'equivalent to rescaling the standard deviation'—I do not see that equivalence. Under what assumptions does absmax scaling approximate standard deviation scaling for blocks?

questions.title: How is zero represented in asymmetric NF4 without wasting a code?
questions.question_body: The paper notes that symmetric $k$-bit quantization lacks an exact zero and then constructs an asymmetric datatype by allocating $2^{k-1}$ negative and $2^{k-1}+1$ positive bins, then 'removing one of the two zeros.' Can someone show the explicit 4-bit NF4 codebook values and explain how an exact zero is guaranteed while preserving equal expected occupancy on negative and positive sides?

questions.title: Double Quantization memory savings: can someone derive the 0.373 bits/parameter reduction?
questions.question_body: For block size 64, first-level scales are FP32, so scales cost $32/64=0.5$ bits/parameter. After double quantization, scales are FP8 per 64-element block and second-level scales are FP32 per 256 first-level scales, leading to $8/64 + 32/(64\cdot 256) = 0.127$ bits/parameter. Can someone walk through these assumptions carefully (e.g., how many scales, exact block partitioning) to reproduce the 0.127 number and thus the 0.373 bits/parameter savings?

questions.title: Does Double Quantization compound dequantization error and how is it controlled?
questions.question_body: Double quantization dequantizes $c_2$ using $c_1$ and then uses that to dequantize $\mathbf{W}$. What is the total expected MSE compared to single-level quantization? Is there a bound that shows the extra distortion from quantizing $c_2$ (with FP8) is negligible relative to the 4-bit weight quantization under typical weight distributions? Any empirical error decomposition or theoretical analysis would help.

questions.title: Backprop through quantized base weights in QLoRA: what gradients are actually computed?
questions.question_body: The method freezes the 4-bit quantized pretrained weights $\mathbf{W}$ and only updates LoRA params $\mathbf{L}_1, \mathbf{L}_2$. The paper says 'the calculation of $\partial E/\partial \mathbf{L}_i$ entails the calculation of $\partial \mathbf{X}/\partial \mathbf{W}$' via dequantization in BF16. Can someone clarify the computational graph? Are we just using dequantized $\mathbf{W}^{\text{BF16}}$ to compute standard GEMM backward to obtain input gradients for upstream layers, while not materializing $\partial E/\partial \mathbf{W}$?

questions.title: Why is $\partial \mathbf{X}/\partial \mathbf{W}$ needed to compute $\partial E/\partial \mathbf{L}_i$?
questions.question_body: Equation (5) defines $\mathbf{Y} = \mathbf{X} \cdot \text{doubleDequant}(\cdot) + s\,\mathbf{X}\mathbf{L}_1\mathbf{L}_2$. I would expect $\partial E/\partial \mathbf{L}_i$ to depend on $\mathbf{X}$ and the upstream gradient $\partial E/\partial \mathbf{Y}$, not on $\partial \mathbf{X}/\partial \mathbf{W}$. Is the point that, for earlier layers' adapters, the upstream gradients require propagating through the frozen base weights (hence we need the backward pass through $\mathbf{W}$ to get $\partial E/\partial \mathbf{X}$), but we do not update $\mathbf{W}$? A small toy backward pass could clarify this.

questions.title: Compute overhead: does dequantize-to-BF16 every forward/backward make QLoRA as fast as 16-bit?
questions.question_body: The introduction claims QLoRA 'does not degrade the runtime' compared to 16-bit finetuning. Intuitively, each matmul needs a dequantization step from NF4 to BF16, and the backward also needs dequantization to compute GEMM gradients. Are these costs overlapped or fused with GEMM in custom CUDA kernels? Under what batch sizes and sequence lengths does QLoRA match or surpass 16-bit runtime?

questions.title: Paged Optimizers and determinism: can unified memory paging change results?
questions.question_body: Paged optimizers rely on CUDA unified memory to page optimizer states between CPU and GPU under memory pressure. Does this introduce nondeterminism due to timing-dependent page faults or different reduction orders? Are there any observed changes in convergence or reproducibility compared to regular in-GPU optimizers? Any seeds/flags that ensure determinism?

questions.title: Which exact linear layers receive LoRA adapters to match 16-bit performance?
questions.question_body: The paper says 'adapters at every network layer' were crucial, but prior LoRA practice often only adapts $W_q$ and $W_v$. For LLaMA-style blocks, do you insert adapters into $W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o$ and also the MLP ($W_{\text{up}}$, $W_{\text{gate}}$, $W_{\text{down}}$)? Are embeddings and the LM head adapted as well? A precise list per transformer block would help reproduce the results.

questions.title: LoRA rank $r$ mattered less than the number of adapted layers—why?
questions.question_body: Figure \ref{fig:hyper} suggests that using adapters in more places matters more than increasing rank $r$. Is there an intuitive explanation (e.g., distributed capacity across transformations beats concentrating rank in fewer spots)? Do you have ablations showing similar performance for $r \in \{4,8,16,32\}$ once all linear layers are adapted?

questions.title: How do the memory numbers add up for a 7B model: 4-bit weights at 5,048 MB?
questions.question_body: For LLaMA-7B, naive 4-bit storage for 7B parameters would be $7\times10^9\times4\,\text{bits} \approx 3.5\,\text{GB}$. The paper reports 5,048 MB for the 4-bit base model, which presumably includes quantization constants and other buffers. Can someone show a rough accounting: weights, first-level scales (with and without double quantization), second-level scales, possible padding/alignments, and any extra buffers needed during forward/backward?

questions.title: How were blocks of size 64 (weights) and 256 (second-level scales) chosen?
questions.question_body: There is a trade-off between smaller blocks (better local scaling, lower quantization error) and more overhead from scales. Do you have a sweep over block sizes (32, 64, 128) showing MSE or downstream task performance vs memory? Similarly, why 256 for the second-level scale block? Any guidance for other architectures (e.g., T5) or smaller/larger models?

questions.title: If scales normalize magnitude, why does NF4 still outperform FP4 and Int4?
questions.question_body: Intuitively, blockwise scaling removes global magnitude differences, so why does the particular placement of codebook levels (NF4 vs FP4 vs Int4) still matter so much? Is it because NF4 places more resolution near the mode and tails according to $N(0,1)$ quantiles, thus better matching the weight distribution even after block scaling? Any visualization of density vs codebook bins would help.

questions.title: Are activations quantized during QLoRA finetuning, or only weights?
questions.question_body: The paper describes quantizing pretrained model weights to 4-bit storage and dequantizing to BF16 for compute. Are activations always in BF16 during forward/backward? If so, are activation outliers (which are common) irrelevant to QLoRA because only weights are quantized? Would activation quantization further reduce memory or hurt training stability?

questions.title: How does QLoRA avoid the training instabilities reported for quantized training?
questions.question_body: Wortsman et al. report stability issues when backpropagating through quantized layers and propose SwitchBack layers. QLoRA claims to be stable at large scale. Is the key difference that QLoRA dequantizes weights to BF16 for compute (so the math is high precision) while only using 4-bit for storage? Or do you also rely on optimizer/hyperparameter choices to ensure stability?

questions.title: Is the NF4 codebook universal across layers and models?
questions.question_body: Since NF4 is derived from the standard normal $N(0,1)$, is the same 4-bit codebook used for all layers, all models, and all training runs? Or do you recompute quantiles per model or per layer? Given you rescale each block to $[-1,1]$ via absmax, does a fixed global NF4 codebook always remain appropriate?

questions.title: How does the asymmetric NF4 ensure an exact zero code for padding and sparsity?
questions.question_body: Padding and exact zeros are important to represent without error. The paper states the asymmetric construction provides a discrete zero. Could someone show how the zero code is chosen and how this interacts with blockwise absmax scaling (e.g., if a block is all zeros, how are scales defined and does dequant preserve exact zeros)?

questions.title: Why does finetuning on FLAN v2 help MMLU but hurt Vicuna-style chat, and vice versa?
questions.question_body: The paper observes that finetuning on FLAN v2 boosts MMLU but performs poorly on Vicuna chat benchmarks, while OASST1/Chip2 yield better chat performance but weaker MMLU. Is this primarily due to task format mismatch (MCQ vs open-ended), instruction style, or domain coverage? Any analysis of training data properties that predict gains on specific benchmarks?

questions.title: How are ties handled when computing Elo ratings from pairwise comparisons?
questions.question_body: You use 3-way labels (model A wins, model B wins, tie) with Elo. The classic Elo update assumes binary outcomes. Which tie handling scheme do you use (e.g., half-point for each, or a modified logistic)? Could you provide the exact update formula and how you aggregate over many prompts and random seeds?

questions.title: GPT-4 evaluator bias: how large is the self-preference and how can it be mitigated?
questions.question_body: The paper reports GPT-4 assigns significantly higher Elo to its own outputs compared to human raters (roughly equivalent to a ~20% win-probability boost). Did you try prompt randomization, anonymizing models, or blinded comparisons to reduce such bias? Any measurements of how much order randomization and double-order averaging reduce the bias?

questions.title: Numerical safety: can NF4 dequantization to BF16 cause overflow/underflow issues?
questions.question_body: Given blockwise absmax scaling, some blocks may have extremely small or large scales. When mapping NF4 codes back to BF16 for GEMM, do you guard against numerical issues (e.g., denormals or overflow)? Any clamping or scale floor/ceiling used in practice? Have you observed NaNs or infs due to dequantization under long sequences and large batch sizes?

questions.title: Why subtract the mean from positive quantization scales before FP8 quantization in DQ?
questions.question_body: The second-level quantization operates on the (positive) first-level scales $c_2$. The paper says to subtract the mean from $c_2$ 'to center the values around zero and make use of symmetric quantization.' Could you provide the exact formula for dequantization in this case (i.e., how do you re-add the mean after dequantizing the centered FP8 values), and explain why centering helps versus using an asymmetric FP8 scheme?

questions.title: Is NF4 optimal under MSE or some rate–distortion criterion?
questions.question_body: Quantile quantization equalizes bin probabilities under a given distribution, but Lloyd–Max quantization for MSE under a Gaussian gives nonuniform bin widths with reconstruction points at conditional means. Is NF4 equivalent to a Lloyd–Max solution for $N(0,1)$ under MSE for $k=4$? If not, which 'information-theoretic' objective does NF4 optimize, and how does its MSE compare to a true Lloyd–Max 4-bit Gaussian quantizer?

questions.title: Can QLoRA work with 3-bit GPTQ weights and still recover 16-bit performance?
questions.question_body: The paper suggests future work exploring more aggressive quantization (e.g., 3-bit). If the base model weights are 3-bit GPTQ and adapters are BF16, do you expect adapter finetuning to recover the accuracy gap? What failure modes might appear (e.g., excessive dequant error, gradient mismatch), and would smaller blocks or learned per-channel scales be required?

questions.title: Which optimizers are supported with paged states, and what are the trade-offs?
questions.question_body: You introduce 'Paged Optimizers' using unified memory. Which optimizers did you implement and test (e.g., AdamW, Adafactor, Adam8bit)? Is there extra overhead when paging momentum/variance buffers in and out? Any known issues with large sequence lengths or gradient accumulation steps that cause thrashing?

questions.title: What patterns of sequence lengths trigger the unified memory paging spikes?
questions.question_body: The paper says memory spikes occur when processing a mini-batch with a long sequence length. Can you characterize the spike magnitude versus sequence length and batch size, and how quickly unified memory responds? Do you recommend specific batching or bucketing strategies to avoid pathological paging behavior?

questions.title: Does double quantization complicate integration with FSDP/ZeRO sharding?
questions.question_body: If using Fully Sharded Data Parallel or ZeRO, how are the two-level scales sharded and communicated? Does double quantization change parameter partitioning or require custom state_dict handling? Any pitfalls when combining QLoRA (with NF4 + DQ) and distributed training strategies?

questions.title: What scaling factor $s$ (or $\alpha$) do you use for LoRA adapters in QLoRA?
questions.question_body: Standard LoRA often uses $\Delta W = (\alpha/r) A B$ with scaling $\alpha$. The paper denotes a scalar $s$ but does not specify the value or schedule. What $s$ (or $\alpha$) and ranks $r$ did you use at 7B/13B/33B/65B, and did you tie or vary $s$ across layers? Any sensitivity to $s$ when adapters are placed in all linear layers?
